name: Freehostia
tagline: Free ad-free hosting plus low-cost cluster-based paid shared plans
description: Freehostia offers a genuinely free, ad-free hosting tier alongside budget paid shared plans on its own Hepsia control panel, running on a load-balanced server cluster.
about: Freehostia is a budget host operated by LiquidNet and best known for its free "Chocolate" plan — a no-cost tier that hosts up to 5 domains with 250MB of disk space, 6GB of monthly bandwidth, a 10MB MySQL database limit and a 2MB maximum upload size, with no forced advertising. It's a genuinely usable option for a small static site, a portfolio, or testing a project, but the storage and bandwidth ceilings mean even a modest WordPress blog will outgrow it quickly — this is not a substitute for a real hosting plan once a site gets any real traffic.

For paid hosting, Freehostia runs four shared tiers — Watercircle ($3.25/mo), Lovebeat ($5.25/mo), Wildhoney ($8.25/mo) and Supernatural ($10.50/mo) — with disk space, bandwidth, domain slots and email accounts scaling up at each tier, and the top two plans (Wildhoney and Supernatural) offering unlimited disk space, bandwidth, domains and email plus a free domain registration. All plans, free and paid, are managed through Hepsia, Freehostia's own in-house control panel rather than cPanel — it covers site installers, a website builder, an .htaccess generator and similar tools, with a reported zero learning curve for newcomers.

Infrastructure runs on a load-balanced Linux/Apache cluster with separate machines handling web, MySQL, email and storage duties, backed by ZFS and NVMe caching plus ModSecurity, aimed at avoiding the bottlenecks of a single all-in-one server. Freehostia backs its hosting with a 99.9% uptime target and a 30-day money-back guarantee on paid plans.
policies: Freehostia offers a 30-day money-back guarantee on its paid shared hosting plans, alongside a 99.9% server uptime target.

The free Chocolate plan carries no money-back guarantee since no payment is taken, and is subject to the same acceptable-use and inactivity policies as any free hosting tier — check Freehostia's terms of service for specifics before relying on it long-term.
